Combined Pareto-Frontier Plot Across Configurations Sharing a Passing Set

Source: R/plot_pareto_combined.R
plot_pareto_combined.Rd

For two or more forestsearch fits whose consistency-passing candidate sets are identical, produces a single Pareto-frontier plot annotated with one S<i>: <combo_label> marker per configuration at each selected subgroup. If two configurations pick the same subgroup, the markers stack into a single multi-line label (e.g.\ "S1: hrMaxSG/pareto\nS2: hrMaxSG/both").

Usage

plot_pareto_combined(
  fs_list,
  combo_labels = NULL,
  ci_table_list = NULL,
  show_band = TRUE,
  xlim = NULL,
  tolerance = 1e-06,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

fs_list

A list of forestsearch result objects. Length must be >= 2.

combo_labels

Character vector of length length(fs_list). Used in the S<i>: <label> annotations. Default NULL = auto, e.g.\ "config 1", "config 2", ...

ci_table_list

Optional list of CI tables from compute_frontier_cis, parallel to fs_list. When provided and the tables match (within tolerance), the CI bars are drawn using the first table.

show_band

Logical. Draw the effect-band shading if applicable. Default TRUE.

xlim

Numeric vector of length 2 or NULL. Default NULL = auto-range.

tolerance

Numeric. Per-cell tolerance for the value equality check (hr, N, E, K). Default 1e-6.

verbose

Logical. Emit a warning naming the specific equality-check failure mode when the sets don't match. Default TRUE.

Value

A ggplot object, or NULL (with a warning) if the passing sets don't satisfy the equality criterion.

Details

The combined plot is meaningful only when the passing sets match. When they don't, the function returns NULL with a warning; the side-by-side view (one panel per configuration) is the appropriate alternative.

Equality criterion

Two passing sets are considered equal when, after sorting by subgroup definition string:

  • they have the same number of rows;

  • the same set of subgroup definitions (concatenated M.* columns), compared as sets (order-independent);

  • within each matched definition, the hr, N, E, and K values agree within tolerance.

Pcons is deliberately excluded from the value check. It can legitimately drift across rules because the preview sort (which depends on selection_rule) changes the queue order, which changes the random-split state each candidate consumes. Drift of up to ~0.10 between runs on the same subgroup is expected and does not indicate a real disagreement. Note also that the internal candidate id m can differ across configurations for the same reason; m is NOT used for equality.

See also

compare_selection_rules, plot_pareto_frontier, pareto_frontier_table.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
out <- compare_selection_rules(
  df.analysis    = actg_df,
  sg_focus       = c("hrMaxSG", "hrMaxSG"),
  selection_rule = c("pareto",  "both"),
  ...
)

# Auto-attached by compare_selection_rules():
print(out$plot_combined)

# Or call directly:
p <- plot_pareto_combined(
  fs_list       = out$fs,
  combo_labels  = out$combos$label,
  ci_table_list = out$ci_tab
)
print(p)
} # }
